battle.name: 高士達起義
battle.brief: 大業七年（611）冬，渤海人高士達在遼東柳城聚眾為盜，眾至數萬，攻陷郡縣，並與山東清河張金稱相呼應，使隋廷腹背受敵。隋將段達討之不克，後楊義臣率遼東還兵擊破之，陣斬張金稱。卡面的斯巴達長矛屬希臘方陣工藝，不在此役現場；同期隋軍步卒用槊與盾列陣，渤海、契丹部眾則以長矛、骨鏃弓應戰。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 大業七年（611）冬，起事於遼東的這場叛亂，交戰的兩方是隋朝中央政府，與以渤海（靺鞨）部眾為主、聯合契丹騎士及漢地流亡戶組成的武裝聯軍。起事時間一般繫於大業七年冬十一月，但逐月明記的文獻有限。隋朝一方由煬帝楊廣直接下詔調度，徵發行軍總管與將軍，率邊軍、郡兵與州府給養的雜役出擊，統兵者先後為段達與楊義臣；義臣以檢校趙郡太守、左光祿大夫的名位率遼東還兵作戰，兵權集中於中央調度，糧秣則自河北、山東沿海路北運，前線指揮與後方補給拉得極長。反方沒有正式國號、沒有編制、沒有固定都城，只憑首領高士達一人號召，渤海、契丹諸部與漢地聚眾鬆散地合在一起，靠攻掠郡縣取得倉廩、鐵器與馬匹，並與山東清河起兵的張金稱南北呼應，令隋廷腹背受敵。隋廷把它當作邊患來平，叛軍則利用高句麗大軍壓境造成的空檔，把邊地部落、逃戶與地方豪強捲進同一場動亂；雙方都沒有可以互相對照的正規戰爭機器。
countriesEn: This rebellion broke out in Liaodong in the winter of Daye 7 (611), and it was fought between the Sui central government on one side and, on the other, an armed coalition formed mainly from the Bohai (Mohe) tribes together with Khitan riders and Han Chinese fugitives from the interior. The outbreak is generally placed in the eleventh month of the winter of Daye 7, though the surviving record is thin on the exact month. On the Sui side the orders came straight from Emperor Yang of Sui, who mobilised column commanders and generals with frontier garrisons, provincial troops and the mixed auxiliaries maintained by the prefectures. The commanders in the field were first Duan Da and later Yang Yichen, the latter fighting with the Liaodong returning army while holding the titles of Inspector of Zhao Commandery and Left Grand Master of Ceremonies. Command was centralised in the capital and grain was carried north from Hebei and Shandong along a road many hundreds of li long, so that command at the front and supply at the rear were stretched to breaking point. The insurgents had no state name, no establishment, no fixed capital: they rallied only to the word of the leader Gao Shida, with the Bohai, Khitan and Han elements loosely joined, taking grain, iron and horses by raiding commandery seats, and answering in sympathy with Zhang Jincheng, who had risen in Qinghe in Shandong, so that the court was squeezed from two directions at once. The court treated the rising as a frontier disorder to be stamped out; the insurgents exploited the vacuum created by the Goguryeo war to draw steppe tribes, deserters and local strongmen into the same disturbance. Neither side had a regular war machine that could be set against the other.
people: 高士達是渤海（靺鞨）人，《隋書》直書「渤海高士達」，起事時在遼東柳城一帶聚眾為盜，眾至數萬，成為隋末第一批起義中唯一以邊地部族為主體的首領。與他同時起事的清河人張金稱在山東響應，隋書把兩人並列記載，可見南北兩處騷動出自同一種壓力。隋將段達最先奉詔討伐，一戰不克；這說明剛從高句麗前線撤回的邊軍在士氣、糧秣與地形適應上都佔下風，冒進反而折損。真正扭轉局面的是關西名將楊義臣：他熟稔西北部眾作戰的兇悍，也熟悉遼東山川，率遼東還兵數萬直搗叛軍，陣中斬張金稱，隨後收合降眾編入行伍，循著降眾指路深入豆子澗，掃平另一名首領格謙。楊廣對義臣的戰功並不安然，怕他威名過盛、急召入朝並升授禮部尚書，義臣不久卒官，而叛軍由此再盛。煬帝本人自洛陽經涿郡渡鴨綠水攻平壤，全部注意力壓在高句麗戰線，這才是這場起義得以長期延續的關鍵背景。
peopleEn: Gao Shida was a Bohai (Mohe) man. The History of Sui records him plainly as Gao Shida of the Bohai; when he rose in the region of Liucheng in Liaodong he drew tens of thousands of followers and became the only leader in the first wave of Sui-end uprisings whose base was a steppe people rather than a Han peasantry. Zhang Jincheng of Qinghe rose in Shandong at the same time, and the History of Sui lists the two together, which shows that the disturbances in the north and in the south grew from the same pressure. The Sui general Duan Da received the first commission to suppress the rising and failed in a single engagement, which tells us that troops coming back from the Goguryeo front were inferior in morale, in supply and in their grasp of the country, and that an advance only cost them men. The man who turned the situation was Yang Yichen, a famous general from the western marches, who knew both the ferocity of northern steppe warfare and the terrain of Liaodong. He led several tens of thousands of returning Liaodong troops straight against the insurgents, cut down Zhang Jincheng in the fighting, then gathered the surrendered men into the ranks and followed their guidance into the Douzi ravine, where he took the other leader Ge Qian alive. Emperor Yang was not at ease about that success, feared Yichen's growing renown, and called him abruptly to the capital and promoted him to Minister of Rites; Yichen died in office shortly after, and the insurgents rose again. Yang Guang himself, marching from Luoyang through Zhuojun and across the Yalu River towards Pyongyang, had his whole attention fixed on the Goguryeo front, and that is the decisive background to why this rising could run for years.
kits: 這張卡面畫的是斯巴達長矛（dory）：約兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套，源於公元前八世紀的希臘世界，在方陣之中靠密集的矛線決定誰站得住。它並沒有出現在遼東——希臘的長槊從未越過亞洲內陸到渤海之濱，這一點必須說清楚。真正在場的是同一門工藝的另一批長柄兵器：隋軍步卒依《隋書·兵志》所載以槊為主，配盾、鑿、鉞之屬，列陣時以槊遮蔽前列、以盾承其矢，車陣中更有以長槊構成向外翻出矛牆的卻月之陣；渤海、契丹部眾所用的長矛與弓箭更為粗獷，弓矢用骨為鏃，另有髀石可擲，遠近兼施。渤海、契丹的騎兵善奔射，隋軍則以驃騎、玄甲等重騎與步騎混編應戰，攻城一方備有雲梯、撞車、巢車與投石砲類器械，守城一方則倚城堞、穴地與木壘塞。同一門工藝，在兩千多年後的遼東雪原與丘陵上依然決定著接觸時誰能站穩——這正是本卡把希臘長矛放到這場起義上來講的理由。
kitsEn: The card shows a Spartan dory: a wooden spear about two metres long with a bronze ferrule at the butt, native to the Greek world of the eighth century BC, where it decided in the phalanx who would still be standing. It was not present in Liaodong: Greek long spears never travelled across the interior of Asia to the shores of the Bohai Sea, and that has to be said plainly. What was actually on the ground was another batch of long-hafted weapons of the same craft. Sui infantry, as the Weapon Treatise of the History of Sui records, fought with the suo as their principal arm, paired with shields, picks and axes, the suo masking the front rank while the shield took the arrows, and in wagon formations there was the queyue array, its long spears opened outward into a wall of points. The long spears and bows of the Bohai and Khitan were rougher affairs, their arrows barbed with bone, with hip-stones thrown by hand so that they could strike at both ranges. The mounted archery of the Bohai and Khitan was formidable, and the Sui answered with armoured and unarmoured cavalry brigades fighting in mixed order; the besiegers had scaling ladders, battering carts, siege towers and stone-throwing engines, while the defenders relied on parapets, tunnels and timber blockhouses. The same craft, in the snows and hills of Liaodong more than two millennia later, still decided who could stand at contact - which is precisely why this card sets a Greek long spear beside this rebellion.
tactics: 大業七年的遼東正處在隋軍主力渡鴨綠水的前線：主力北上攻高句麗，遼東各郡的守備空虛，這是叛軍得以迅速攻陷郡縣的前提。渤海與契丹部眾熟悉本地道路，多游走於山林、丘陵與河谷之間，以小隊騎射擾亂隋軍糧道，不與隋軍正面列陣；攻守城邑時則驅使步卒持長矛與盾逼近牆根，破壞守軍的結陣。隋將段達統兵直進，在缺乏準備、糧秣接應不上的情況下與叛軍交鋒而敗績，說明以游擊消耗隋軍的戰法一度奏效，也說明遠征歸來的邊軍在陌生戰場上不適合強攻。義臣接手後改取硬打：他以嫻熟部眾戰法又熟悉遼東地形的長處，率遼東還兵數萬直搗叛軍本營，一戰而破，陣斬張金稱；隨後收合降眾、編為行伍，循降眾指路深入豆子澗的巢穴，掃平格謙一伙。義軍的長處是熟悉地形、來去如風，短處是組織鬆散、缺乏攻城器械，一旦被主力咬住而無法走脫，就容易在會戰中被吞掉。
tacticsEn: Liaodong in Daye 7 sat directly behind the Sui main army as it crossed the Yalu River: with the bulk of the field force marching north against Goguryeo, the garrisons of the Liaodong commanderies were left hollow, and that was the premise on which the insurgents overran district seats so quickly. The Bohai and Khitan knew the local roads, moved through hills, woods and river valleys, harried Sui supply columns with small mounted parties, and generally declined to meet the Sui army in a set battle. When towns were attacked they drove footmen forward with long spears and shields to press against the foot of the walls and break up the defenders' formation. Duan Da marched straight in, engaged without preparation and without supply support, and was beaten, which showed both that the war of attrition carried by raiding parties worked for a time and that troops returning from distant campaigns were poor candidates for frontal assault in unfamiliar country. Yichen changed the method and chose to strike hard: he used his mastery of steppe fighting and his knowledge of Liaodong, led several tens of thousands of returning Liaodong troops straight into the heart of the insurgents, broke them in a single action and cut down Zhang Jincheng; then he gathered the surrendered men into the ranks and followed their guidance into the strongholds of the Douzi ravine, clearing out Ge Qian and his followers. The strength of the insurgents lay in knowing the country and moving like wind; their weakness lay in loose organisation and a lack of siege equipment, and once the main army closed on them and cut off their retreat they tended to be swallowed in a pitched battle.
data: 關於兵數，現存記載多而確數少。《隋書》說高士達、張金稱「相聚為盜，眾已數萬，攻陷郡縣」，又說義臣率「遼東還兵數萬」擊破之，兩處都用「數萬」一語而不給確數，《資治通鑑》一系的記載與此相近，諸說並存，無法核對。較可計數的是隋軍攻高句麗的規模：史載大業七年出師兵馬五十餘萬，一次用糧至一百五十萬石，往後續增至三百萬石與五百萬石，道路上的輜重與民夫遠多於作戰部隊。此類數字歷來被認為有所誇張，但足以說明遼東戰線的負擔之重，使前線一有後院起火，朝廷便無力兩頭兼顧。距離方面，柳城（營州治所，今遼寧朝陽）距襄平（遼陽）約二百餘里，豆子澗一帶在海城與鞍山之間，隋軍還師、追擊、再轉戰的路線全在這一二百里的範圍內，不必遠征便可窮追。時間上，叛亂起於大業七年冬，義臣平之則在大業十年之後，橫跨數年。義軍首領高士達的生死下落，各史均無明文記載。
dataEn: On numbers, the surviving record is rich in approximations and poor in certainties. The History of Sui says that Gao Shida and Zhang Jincheng gathered together as bandits, that their numbers had already reached tens of thousands and that they had overrun commanderies and counties, and it also says that Yichen took several tens of thousands of returning Liaodong troops and shattered them; both passages use the phrase several tens of thousands without a precise figure, and the Zhizhi Tongjian tradition agrees closely, so the accounts stand side by side and cannot be checked against one another. The scale that can be counted better is that of the Sui war against Goguryeo: the chronicles give the army mustered in Daye 7 as more than half a million men, with one hundred and fifty thousand shi of grain for the first provisioning, later raised to three hundred thousand and then to five hundred thousand, the carts and the labour gangs on the roads far outnumbering the troops who fought. Such figures are generally held to be exaggerated, but they are enough to show how heavy the Liaodong front was, and that once the rear of the empire caught fire the court could not fight on two fronts at once. As for distances: Liucheng, the seat of Yingzhou, lies a little over two hundred li from Xiangping, present-day Liaoyang, and the Douzi ravine lies between Haicheng and Anshan, so the whole cycle of marching back, pursuing and turning to fight again ran within a couple of hundred li and required no distant expedition to run the insurgents down. In time, the rising began in the winter of Daye 7 and was put down by Yichen only after Daye 10, spanning several years. The fate of the insurgent leader Gao Shida himself is nowhere stated in the histories.
cause: 高士達起義的直接導火線，是隋朝把整個東北壓在征高句麗的戰車上。大業七年冬，煬帝大軍北進，前線深入鴨綠水與平壤，遼東各郡同時被徵發兵丁、輜重與馬匹，耕作者離田，倉廩為之一空；高句麗又乘隙出兵襲擾，州縣的守備與生產一同崩壞。渤海、契丹等邊地部眾長期受隋的邊境政策、馬匹交易與使往約束，一旦隋廷把兵力抽調到南方前線，邊防空虛便成為叛軍可以立旗的契機；而中原王朝的民戶在重役之下大批逃亡，逃戶與邊民在遼東山澤間相遇，結合成一支沒有常備軍的武裝。叛軍的號召極為簡單：不高舉大義名分，只以「保境」與「得糧」為由聚眾，攻下郡縣便取其倉廩、鐵器與牲畜，兵眾靠奪來的物資壯大。山東方面張金稱幾乎同時起事，說明這並非邊地孤例，而是隋朝整個財政與兵役體制在多地同時崩開的結果。
causeEn: The immediate spark of Gao Shida's rising was the Sui decision to press the whole of the north-east onto the war machine aimed at Goguryeo. In the winter of Daye 7 the imperial army marched north, the front ran deep towards the Yalu River and Pyongyang, and the commanderies of Liaodong were at the same moment stripped of soldiers, transport animals and remounts, so that the men left the fields and the granaries were emptied; Goguryeo took the opportunity to raid, and the defence and the harvest of the districts collapsed together. The Bohai and Khitan had long been held in place by Sui frontier policy, by the trade in horses and by the constant traffic of envoys, and once the court drew its troops away to the southern front, the empty border became the opening for a revolt. Meanwhile the households of the interior fled the heavy levies in large numbers, and deserters meeting the border folk in the hills and marshes of Liaodong welded themselves into an armed band with no standing army behind it. The insurgents' appeal was extremely plain: they raised no banner of righteous cause, but gathered men under the pretext of defending the district and of getting grain, and when they took a commandery seat they took its granaries, its iron and its cattle, so that the host grew on what it seized. That Zhang Jincheng rose in Shandong almost at the same moment shows this was not an isolated frontier affair but the collapse, in several places at once, of the whole fiscal and conscription system of the Sui.
impact: 這場起義的第一重後果，是隋朝在遼東的邊防體系被打穿。燕郡、襄平、安樂一帶的郡縣秩序陷入混亂，叛軍與隋軍在柳城至豆子澗的山川間拉鋸，隋廷必須從西線與中原抽調兵將回援，結果是前方的高句麗戰役更無力支撐——大業八年與九年的兩次深入都沒有拿下平壤，高句麗得以延續其政權，直到唐太宗貞觀十九年（645）出兵攻安市、唐高宗總章元年（668）才被唐朝先後打倒。第二重後果在制度層面：隋廷以「討賊」為名把兵權散給諸王，煬帝令子弟分鎮諸州，以防地方再叛，這種封王鎮州的做法在隋末迅速演成割據的溫床。第三重後果在族群與疆域：渤海（靺鞨）部族趁亂整合了遼東與吉林一帶的粟末靺鞨各部，於唐武德元年（618）建國、貞觀二年（626）正式用漢式國號渤海，成為唐朝在東北長期競爭的對手；北方人口的流動與部族的重組，也為唐初的東北邊防與營州都督府的設置埋下伏線。
impactEn: The first consequence of this rising was that the Sui frontier system in Liaodong was broken open. Order in the commanderies around Yan, Xiangping and Anle fell apart, and the insurgents and the Sui armies pulled at each other across the hills and streams between Liucheng and the Douzi ravine. The court had to recall generals and soldiers from the western front and from the interior, and the result was that the war against Goguryeo could no longer be sustained: neither the campaign of Daye 8 nor that of Daye 9 brought Pyongyang down, and Goguryeo went on living until Tang Taizong attacked Anshi in Zhenguan 19 (645) and until Tang Gaozong destroyed the kingdom outright in Zongzhang 1 (668). The second consequence was institutional: under the pretext of suppressing bandits the court dispersed military power to the princes, and Yang Guang sent his own sons to hold the various prefectures so that no district might rebel again. What was meant as a remedy hardened into the breeding ground of the warlordism that marked the end of the Sui. The third consequence was ethnic and territorial: the Bohai (Mohe) peoples used the disorder to knit the various Sushen Mohe tribes of Liaodong and western Jilin together, founding a state in Wude 1 (618) and taking the Chinese-style name Bohai in Zhenguan 2 (626), and so becoming a long-term rival of Tang on the north-eastern frontier. The movement of northern populations and the reordering of the tribes in that region also prefigured Tang China's northern defence and the setting up of the Dudufu at Yingzhou.
result: 結局分兩層。就戰役本身：段達首討敗績，高士達眾至數萬，張金稱被斬，格謙於豆子澗被擒，楊義臣以遼東還兵數萬大破叛軍主力，隋廷在戰術上贏了這一仗。然而楊廣怕義臣威名過盛，急召其入朝、升任禮部尚書，叛軍隨即復盛；這說明這場戰爭並未真正結束——一次會戰的勝利替代不了對遼東郡縣的治理，也替代不了對邊地部族的安撫。高士達本人的下落則史無明文：《隋書》只記義臣「大破士達」，並未言其被擒被斬與生死，故此役的收束在文獻上是懸案，諸說並存。往後看，這支部眾的力量逐漸被消耗與分化：山東一路早被平定，高句麗得以坐觀中原內亂，隋朝卻在起義的連續消耗之下於大業十四年（618）崩潰，長江以北盡成群雄割據之勢。渤海部族在隋亡之後迅速整合並建國，高句麗又撐了半個世紀才為唐朝所滅。遼東在隋唐之際的結局，可以說是隋朝失其東北，而新的東北秩序要等到唐朝才重新建立起來。
resultEn: The outcome has two layers. As a campaign: the first Sui commander, Duan Da, was beaten; Gao Shida's host had run to tens of thousands; Zhang Jincheng was cut down; Ge Qian was taken alive in the Douzi ravine; and Yang Yichen, with several tens of thousands of returning Liaodong troops, shattered the main body of the insurgents, so that the court won this battle on the field. Yet Emperor Yang, fearing Yichen's renown, called him abruptly to the capital and made him Minister of Rites, and the insurgents rose again immediately - which shows that the war had not really been ended, because one victory in the field could replace neither the government of the Liaodong commanderies nor the pacification of the steppe peoples. Gao Shida's own fate is nowhere recorded: the History of Sui says only that Yichen broke him badly, without saying whether he was taken, killed or survived, so the closing of this rising is a suspended question in the literature and the accounts stand side by side. Looking further ahead, the armed band was gradually spent and split: the Shandong wing had been stamped out early, Goguryeo was able to sit and watch the empire tear itself apart in the interior, and the Sui, worn down by one rising after another, collapsed in Daye 14 (618), leaving everything north of the Yangtze in the hands of contending warlords. The Bohai peoples integrated themselves and founded a state soon after the fall of the Sui, and Goguryeo survived another half century before Tang destroyed it. The end of the story in Liaodong across the Sui-Tang hinge is that the Sui lost its north-east, and a new order for that frontier had to wait for the Tang to build it.
